title: Filter Far More, Take Most Back

scenes.visual: Title card 'Filter Far More, Take Most Back' over a cartoon kidney bean shape in soft red. COLOUR MAP for both films: blood RED; filtrate and urine YELLOW (amber); salt ORANGE dots; water BLUE drops; glucose GREEN squares; drug PURPLE diamonds; tissue saltiness a light-to-dark ORANGE shading (saltier = darker). Everything is a schematic cartoon labelled 'schematic'.

scenes.tts: Every day, your kidneys filter about one hundred and eighty litres of plasma. Yet you pass only one or two litres of urine. Why would an organ filter so much more than it lets go?
scenes.caption: Every day, your kidneys filter about 180 litres of plasma. Yet you pass only one or two litres of urine. Why would an organ filter so much more than it lets go?
scenes.visual: Left: a tall YELLOW column fills upward, label '180 L filtered per day (adult human)'. Right: a short YELLOW column rises to a fraction of its height, label '1 to 2 L urine per day'. A question mark pulses between them. Bars drawn to scale.
scenes.narration: Every day, your kidneys filter about 180 litres of plasma. Yet you pass only one or two litres of urine. Why would an organ filter so much more than it lets go?

scenes.tts: The kidney's working unit is the nephron: a filter attached to a long tube. Blood enters a knot of capillaries, the glomerulus, through the afferent arteriole. It leaves through the efferent arteriole.
scenes.visual: One nephron drawn left to right on a pale ledger-paper background: a RED capillary knot at the left inside a cup, then a long tube running right and ending in a duct. A RED vessel flows in (arrow, label 'afferent arteriole: in') and a RED vessel flows out (label 'efferent arteriole: out'). Labels 'nephron', 'glomerulus'.
scenes.narration: The kidney's working unit is the nephron: a filter attached to a long tube. Blood enters a knot of capillaries, the glomerulus, through the afferent arteriole. It leaves through the efferent arteriole.

scenes.tts: Blood pressure pushes plasma through a barrier into Bowman's capsule, the cup around the capillaries. This fluid is the filtrate. It carries water, salt, glucose and urea, but no blood cells and very little protein.
scenes.visual: Zoom on the cup (label 'Bowman's capsule'). BLUE drops, ORANGE dots, GREEN squares and small grey 'urea' dots squeeze through a dashed barrier into the cup, forming a YELLOW stream into the tube. RED blood cells and large grey blobs labelled 'protein' bounce off the barrier and stay in the RED capillaries. Label 'filtrate'.
scenes.narration: Blood pressure pushes plasma through a barrier into Bowman's capsule, the cup around the capillaries. This fluid is the filtrate. It carries water, salt, glucose and urea, but no blood cells and very little protein.

scenes.tts: From here on, the tube does two jobs. It takes substances back into the blood. That is reabsorption. It also adds substances from the blood. That is secretion. So keep a ledger. What leaves in urine is what was filtered, minus what was taken back, plus what was added.
scenes.visual: RED capillaries now wrap the tube. Arrows from tube to capillary appear, label 'reabsorbed (taken back)'; arrows from capillary into tube appear, label 'secreted (added)'. A ledger bar types itself across the top of the screen: 'excreted = filtered - reabsorbed + secreted', each term lighting as it is spoken.
scenes.narration: From here on, the tube does two jobs. It takes substances back into the blood. That is reabsorption. It also adds substances from the blood. That is secretion. So keep a ledger. What leaves in urine is what was filtered, minus what was taken back, plus what was added.

scenes.tts: Run three substances through the same ledger. First, glucose. It is filtered at about its level in plasma. The proximal tubule, the first stretch of tube, normally takes almost all of it back. Almost none is left to leave.
scenes.visual: GREEN squares enter the capsule with the filtrate. Along the first stretch (label 'proximal tubule') nearly all hop back into the RED capillaries; one faint GREEN square drifts on, label 'schematic'. Ledger row fills: 'glucose: freely filtered; nearly all taken back; almost none excreted'.
scenes.narration: Run three substances through the same ledger. First, glucose. It is filtered at about its level in plasma. The proximal tubule, the first stretch of tube, normally takes almost all of it back. Almost none is left to leave.

scenes.tts: Next, sodium. The proximal tubule takes back about sixty to seventy percent of the filtered sodium, and water follows it. Later stretches of the tube take back more. Only a small share is left to leave.
scenes.caption: Next, sodium. The proximal tubule takes back about 60 to 70% of the filtered sodium, and water follows it. Later stretches of the tube take back more. Only a small share is left to leave.
scenes.visual: ORANGE dots flow in; in the proximal tubule about two-thirds hop back to the RED capillaries, each with BLUE drops trailing after it; label '60 to 70% of filtered sodium'. Further along, more ORANGE dots hop back. A thin trickle of ORANGE reaches the exit. Ledger row: 'sodium: most taken back'.
scenes.narration: Next, sodium. The proximal tubule takes back about 60 to 70% of the filtered sodium, and water follows it. Later stretches of the tube take back more. Only a small share is left to leave.

scenes.tts: Last, some drugs. They are filtered, and the proximal tubule also secretes them into the tube. So more of the drug can leave than was filtered.
scenes.visual: PURPLE diamonds pass the filter into the tube. In the proximal tubule, extra PURPLE diamonds jump from the RED capillaries into the tube (arrow 'secreted'). At the exit, the PURPLE stream is wider than at the start. Ledger row: 'some drugs: filtered + secreted'.
scenes.narration: Last, some drugs. They are filtered, and the proximal tubule also secretes them into the tube. So more of the drug can leave than was filtered.

scenes.tts: Now water, the biggest entry of all by volume. Of everything filtered each day, about ninety-nine percent comes back to the blood. So the filter does not set how much urine you make. The take-back does.
scenes.caption: Now water, the biggest entry of all by volume. Of everything filtered each day, about 99% comes back to the blood. So the filter does not set how much urine you make. The take-back does.
scenes.visual: A broad BLUE stream enters the tube; BLUE drops pour back into the RED capillaries all along it, leaving only a thin YELLOW sliver at the exit. On screen: '180 L filtered', 'about 99% taken back', '1 to 2 L urine'. The word 'take-back' glows on the ledger bar.
scenes.narration: Now water, the biggest entry of all by volume. Of everything filtered each day, about 99% comes back to the blood. So the filter does not set how much urine you make. The take-back does.

scenes.tts: Suppose the tube took back ninety-eight percent of the water instead of ninety-nine. Would urine rise by about one percent, or by much more? Pause and decide.
scenes.caption: Suppose the tube took back 98% of the water instead of 99%. Would urine rise by about 1%, or by much more? Pause and decide.
scenes.visual: Two dials side by side: 'take-back 99%' and 'take-back 98%'. Below each, an empty urine bar. Two answer cards: 'about 1% more urine' and 'much more'.
scenes.narration: Suppose the tube took back 98% of the water instead of 99%. Would urine rise by about 1%, or by much more? Pause and decide.

scenes.visual: Predict pause. Cards hold. A 5-second ring timer at bottom right.

scenes.tts: Much more: urine about doubles. What leaves is a thin sliver of a huge flow. Shift the take-back slightly, and that sliver changes a lot.
scenes.visual: The two urine bars fill, computed from 180 L: 'take-back 99%: 1.8 L' and 'take-back 98%: 3.6 L'. The second bar is twice the first. The 'much more' card lights.
scenes.narration: Much more: urine about doubles. What leaves is a thin sliver of a huge flow. Shift the take-back slightly, and that sliver changes a lot.

scenes.tts: A healthy kidney does not leave this to chance. When filtration rises, the proximal tubule takes back about the same share. Hormones make the fine adjustments in the last stretches, mainly the collecting duct.
scenes.visual: The tube redrawn: the proximal tubule labelled 'takes back about the same share'. The last stretches (labels 'late distal tubule' and 'collecting duct') glow, the collecting duct brightest, with small hormone icons docking on them, label 'fine adjustments'. The urine bar settles back near 1.5 L.
scenes.narration: A healthy kidney does not leave this to chance. When filtration rises, the proximal tubule takes back about the same share. Hormones make the fine adjustments in the last stretches, mainly the collecting duct.

scenes.tts: So the kidney filters a lot, and the take-back largely sets how much water you lose. Glucose, sodium, a drug and water all fit one ledger: filtered, minus taken back, plus added.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the whole nephron with all four ledger rows stacked on the top bar: GREEN, ORANGE, PURPLE, BLUE. The bar 'excreted = filtered - reabsorbed + secreted' stays fixed while the streams loop.
scenes.narration: So the kidney filters a lot, and the take-back largely sets how much water you lose. Glucose, sodium, a drug and water all fit one ledger: filtered, minus taken back, plus added.

scenes.visual: Hex end card. Line: 'The take-back, not the filter, largely sets how much urine leaves.'
